newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-Korean GDRs slide on tension with North.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-Korean GDRs slide on tension with North.

text.p: Korean global depository receipts closed sharply lower Wednesday on news of increased tension between North and South Korea, traders said.
Shares in Seoul fell rapidly, after North Korea warned it was ready for a "final battle" with the U.S. and South Korea, which it accused of preparing to attack the North.
"I don't think people in London were taking it all that seriously but (GDRs) were strong yesterday and it gave back some ground," a trader said.
Rumours of financial troubles in automotive company Kia Group also hung over the market, traders said. Kia affiliate Asia Motors acknowledged on Monday making a late debt payment.
The HSBC James Capel Korea GDR Index closed down 2.49 points, or 3.03 percent, to 79.65 points, a premium of 42.54 percent over the local market.
Seoul's composite stock index eased 19.08 points, or 2.41 percent, to 773.21
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed 1.31 points higher at 89.57, or 1.34 percent, a premium of 30.87 percent over the local market.
State Bank of India, which reports earnings tomorrow, lost six cents to $26.25/$27.00 and Bajaj Auto gained $1.62 to $35.75/$37.25.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index rose 0.67 points, or 0.53 percent, to 127.71, representing a discount to the local market of 2.85 percent.
